rulings.text: He CAN use his ability on a unit or hero that's already exhausted. He CAN use it on units or heroes you control as well.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You will get gold from your workers before you have to pay the cost. Also, since you as the active player decide in what order your upkeep effects happen, you can collect gold from upkeep effects like Galina Glimmer and Gemscout Owl before you have to pay. HOWEVER, you can't play cards or activate abilities (such as Merfolk Prospector and Rickety Mine) until your Main phase, so they can't help you pay the cost.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You still have to pay any additional costs of that card as you play it. For example, if your opponent has a Building Inspector, you pay 1 even if Promise of Payment makes the first building you build cost 0.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Hiring a worker is not playing a card. Building a Tech Building or Add-on isn't playing a card. Using an ability of a card or putting a card into play is not playing a card. Promise of Payment doesn't apply to any of those things.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You CAN use Promise of Payment to play a unit from Graveyard or to play the top card of your draw pile with Vir's middle ability.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Be sure to play Promise of Payment JUST before you play the card you want to pay 0 for. If you play another card in between (even with an effect like Cinderblast Dragon's attack effect), you have to apply Promise of Payment's effect to that card instead.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: The gold cost you have to pay during your next upkeep is the printed gold cost on the card. You don't get to apply any effects that would reduce its cost (even Gigadon's effect that's on the card itself).

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If for some reason you play Promise of Payment and then don't play any other cards that turn, nothing happens during your next upkeeep.

rulings.author: sharpo
rulings.text: Promise of Payment does not help you pay for Boost. If you play Promise of Payment and then Murkwood Allies, you only get one kind of token unless you pay 4 gold.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: She fades away when her last time rune is removed for any reason. Removing the last rune with the Time Spiral spell or her own max level ability will cause her to die.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: "Dies from fading" means that the last time rune she had was removed because the fading ability said to do that during the upkeep. It doesn't trigger if something else removed her last time rune.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If she has exactly two time runes, she CAN use her max level ability to trash a unit. If she does, she then immediately dies because of hanving no fading runes, then the trashed unit returns to play. This does not count as "dies from fading" on her middle ability, because that only triggers if fading itself removed the last time rune.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When her max level ability returns a unit to play, it returns under the control of whoever controlled it when it was trashed.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When her max level ability returns a unit to play, it returns in a "fresh" state. It's a new object, and no longer has any properties of the old object such as +1/+1 runes, damage, being a dance partner from Two Step, etc. It also returns ready (not exhausted) and it can't attack or use exhaust abilities unless it has haste.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If two twins die simultaneously, the active player chooses which returns to your codex.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If the unit or hero has any armor left at the end of the turn, that armor disappears.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Readying one of your units CAN allow it to attack twice in a turn. (Attack with a unit, which will exhaust it. Play Ready or Not on that unit to ready it, then you can attack with it again.)

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If a unit has the readiness keyword, using Ready or Not on it won't let you attack twice in a turn with it because readiness specifically says you can't do that.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If you choose the to "Deal 6 damage to up to 2 units and/or heroes", that means you can hit two units for 6 damage each, two heroes for 6 damage each, or one unit for 6 damage AND one hero for 6 damage. You could also choose to hit just one thing if you want: one unit for 6 damage or one hero for 6 damage.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When you trash an opponent's worker, you don't get to choose which worker to destroy (because they're alll considered identical) and you don't get to see the front of the destroyed worker.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When you "return a unit with fading to play" this way, you don't pay for it.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If the reason you remove a time rune from Rememberer isn't because of the fading ability, but rather something else such as Time Spiral, Seer, or Tinkerer, then Remember's ability to give you a unit with fading from your discard pile still DOES trigger.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If you have just one Rememberer and you remove the last time rune, you CAN return her to play with her own ability. In this situation, the "dies from fading" effect and the "remember" ability trigger simultaneously, so as the active player you can choose the order.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You CAN return a tech III unit to play with this (for free!) but in order to do so, you must have the appropriate spec tech III building fully constructed.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When Newsman leaves play, his effect ends.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You resolve a spell's effect before discarding it, so a given copy of Research & Development cannot draw itself from its own effect. You first draw cards from its effect, and you reshuffle your discard pile into your draw pile if you would draw from empty draw pile. Then, you discard Research & Development when you have finished resolving its effect.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: As a gamewide rule, you can only reshuffle your discard pile into your draw pile once per main phase. The help text on this card is there because it's very possible to "try" to do it more times using this card. If drawing cards during your main phase causes you to reshuffle your discard pile into your draw pile once, then later that same main phase you would draw when you have an empty draw pile, instead you don't. You can't draw any more cards until your draw/discard step.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: The ability triggers from a unit dying, so it means that unit really did die. Anything that triggers from a unit dying really will trigger, such as drawing a card if the unit died when it was in the technician slot.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: This doesn't cause the units to "die", so the opponent won't draw a card if a returned unit was in the technician slot.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You still have to put a card from your hand into the worker zone, even though you don't have to pay gold to hire a worker. And you still can only hire one worker per turn.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If an effect increases the cost of hiring workers, you still have to pay that cost increase. For example, if something increased the cost to hire workers by 1 for all players, you'd pay 1 to hire a worker, while players without Rich Earth would pay 2 to hire workers.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You can't use the ability the turn Rickety Mine comes under your control because it doesn't have haste.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: "Phew!" has no gameplay effect. It has a psychological effect though.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You can only reduce the gold cost of something to 0, not lower than that.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: "Lowest tech unit with least ATK" means first you look at the set of units the lowest tech, such as "tech 0." Tech 0 is below I is below II is below III. Next, choose the unit in that set with the least ATK.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If there are any units that are indestructible or that can't be sacrificed, ignore them when looking for the weakest unit. If such a thing would be your "weakest unit" then instead sacrifice your next weakest.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: After your unit finishes its attack (after combat damage is dealt), it loses the armor Safe Attacking granted if it still had it.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If something readies that unit and you attack with it a second time that turn, it will get 1 point of armor again.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When you put units into play with this ability, you don't have to pay for them and you don't have to meet the tech requirements for them either.

rulings.author: sharpo
rulings.text: The units gain haste and ephemeral permanently. So if they don't leave play after one turn, they'll keep trying to die every turn, and Wandering Mimic will get haste from them.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When this returns a unit to play, it returns in a "fresh" state. It's a new object, and no longer has any properties of the old object such as +1/+1 runes, damage, being a dance partner from Two Step, etc. It also returns ready (not exhausted) and it can't attack or use exhaust abilities unless it has haste.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: This does trigger on opponent's turns. So it can trigger once on your own turn, again on an opponent's turn, then again when it's your following turn, etc.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If you steal a unit with Kidnapping, and this would then "return it to play," it returns under your control, not the original owner's control. "Return" effects check the last controller, rather than the owner.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If one of your TOKEN units leaves play, then it's destroyed as usual. (Tokens can't go to other zones than in play.) This does not use up the "once-per-turn" of Second Chances, so Second Chances will still trigger later than turn if one of your non-token units dies from something other than combat damage.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: The sparkshot ability and the Tower add-on deal combat damage, so if these kill one of your units, Second Chances won't save it. Second Chances will save units affected by Undo, Rewind, Doom Grasp (whether it was the sacrifice effect OR destroy effect!), Hooded Executioner's ability, the obliterate ability, damage from Flame Arrow or Shadow Blade, to name a few.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You can add or remove time runes from things opponents control, if you want.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: The damage done by the sparkshot ability and by the Tower add-on are both combat damage. But they are also both "abilities" so Sentry CAN prevent their damage.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: It's ok to have more than 5 cards in your hand. When you reach the discard/draw phase, you'll still have to discard your hand, and draw that many cards + 2, capped at 5.

rulings.author: sharpo
rulings.text: If you destroy an Illusion because you targeted it with Shadow Blade, its controller discards a card.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You can't discard a card DURING your upkeep to save it from dying from fading. You can only use abilities during your own main phase unless they are specifically marked otherwise, such as "upkeep" abilities.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: "Card draw +1, hand size +1" means that instead of discarding your hand and drawing that many cards +2, capped at 5, you instead discard your hand and draw that many cards +3, capped at 6.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If this would cause simultaneous effects to happen that require some order (such as multiple units dying that have "dies" triggers), then you (the active player) choose the order.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You can target two units, two heroes, or one unit and one hero. You can also choose to have just one target if you want: just one unit or just one hero.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Copying something copies the printed version of the card and does not copy any modifiers. For example, if you copy a 2/2 that has a +1/+1 rune on it and Spirit of the Panda attached to it, the copy will just be a 2/2.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If an effect changes the "printed" values of a card, the new values will be used. This includes Chaos Mirror and transformation effects such as Polymorph: Squirrel.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: For both middle ability and max level ability, the copy is an Illusion. That means, for example, if you copy a unit of type Squirrel or Mystic then the copy will be an Illusion Squirrel or an Illusion Mystic. It will still count as a Squirrel or Mystic, and it also counts as an Illusion. Because it's an Illusion, it dies if its targeted.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If you use the middle ability or max level ability to make of your Mirror Illusions a copy of something else, you can't use either of those abilities again the same turn on that same Illusion. The reason is that the ability refers to your "Mirror Illusion" but after your Mirror Illusion copies a Squirrel, for example, you have an Illusion Squirrel, not a Mirror Illusion. You can use these abilities on ANOTHER Mirror Illusion you control though.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Mirror Illusions that are copying something else DO still count toward your limit of 2 Mirror Illusion tokens.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: The max level ability says that when you use it to make one of your Mirror Illusions copy something, you must trash it when Quince or the thing it copied leaves. This does NOT have anything to do with Mirror Illusions that have not yet copied anything. Mirror Illusions that haven't copied anything do NOT get trashed when Quince leaves.

rulings.author: sharpo
rulings.text: Quince's middle ability trashes the Mirror Illusion only once at the end of the turn you use the ability.

rulings.author: sharpo
rulings.text: Quince's max level ability can try to trash the Mirror Illusion two times, once when Quince leaves and once when the unit copied by the Mirror Illusion leaves.

rulings.author: sharpo
rulings.text: If your Mirror Illusion copies a Tech 1 unit, it becomes Tech 1.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When you put a unit into play with this ability, you don't have to pay for it and you don't have to meet the tech requirements for it either. It even allows you to put a tech III unit into play.

rulings.author: sharpo
rulings.text: You can pay the cost for Skeletal Lord's ability using skeletons that came under your control this turn.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: For example, if a player had 7 workers, they would get a total of 4 gold from their workers, rather than 7 gold.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When Smoker is targeted by something, he immediately returns to hand, even before the rest of the spell or ability that targeted him resolves.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Whenever heroes enter a command zone, they lose all levels (become level 1) and other properties. They lose any damage on them, lose +1/+1 runes, lose any attachments, etc.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When Snapback returns a hero to its command zone, it cannot put that very same hero back into play unless there are no other heroes at all in that command zone.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When Snapback returns a hero to its command zone, it CAN return a different hero from that command zone to play, even if that different hero is currently on cooldown from dying somehow.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When the attached unit "would die," it doesn't actually die so things that trigger on "dies" such as drawing a card in the technician slot don't happen.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If you Soul Stone something with Two Lives such as Justice Juggernaut or Garus Rook, then the first time it would die, it gets a crumbling rune from the Two Lives ability instead. The second time it would die, Soul Stone's ability triggers (effectively giving it a third life)

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: "He can only spar" means that if you use his second ability, he can still use his first ability that same turn, even though he can't attack for the rest of that turn.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If you aren't able to target an opposing Flagbearer for any reason, you don't have to. That includes if the Flagbearer has "resist 1" and you have no gold. In that case, you can't target it with a spell or ability because you can't afford to pay the cost for resist, so you can ignore the Flagbearer and target something else.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Removing a +1/+1 rune can cause Spore Shambler to die if he ends up with 0 or less HP (in other words, if he has damage on him greater than or equal to his HP).

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: To pay the cost of "remove a +1/+1" rune, you must remove the rune from Spore Shambler, not from something else.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Units that have overpower do not LOSE overpower from this spell, so a Wandering Mimic would still see those units as having the keyword. It's just that Stampedes instructions for where to send the excess damage happen, and overpower's instructions don't.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If you have a healing effect during your upkeep from another card such as Helpful Turtle, you, as the active player, can choose the order of your upkeep effects. So you can choose to heal Star-Crossed Starlet BEFORE she takes 1 damage from her own upkeep ability in that case.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Normally, Star-Crossed Starlet can have only 1 damage on her (and therefore +1 ATK from her ability) without dying. 2 damage is enough to kill her. But if she has a +1/+1 rune on her, for example from Bloom, then she has a total of 3 HP and can therefore have 2 damage on her (and +2 ATK from her ability) without dying.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: This doesn't cause the unit to "die", so the opponent won't draw a card if it was in the technician slot.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: His ability does nothing against an opponent that doesn't have any gold.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: The "if you do" clause of Temporal Distortion is not satisfied if you try to return a unit to your hand, but it can't be returned, such as a Gilded Glaxx that "can't leave play."

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Tokens are generally tech 0, so they usually can't be returned to your hand for this effect. However, if you have a token that's copying a tech I or II unit, you CAN choose to return it to your hand for this spell. It will be destroyed as it would go into your hand, but the "if you do" clause of Temporal Distortion is satisfied. You really can still put a unit from your codex into play (based on the cost and tech level of the unit that token was copying).

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: The time runes on your forecasted cards count too, even though those are "in the future" and not in play. Time runes from fading or from Tricycloid also count.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You resolve a spell's effect before discarding it, so Temporal Research cannot draw itself from its own effect. You first draw cards from Temporal Research's effect, and you reshuffle your discard pile into your draw pile if you would draw from empty draw pile. Then, you discard Temporal Research when you have finished resolving its effect.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: The Warlock tokens are controlled by the chosen opponent. That opponent can sacrifice them, patrol with them, attack with them, etc.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: A particular copy of Terras Q is only shackled by the Warlocks that HE put into play. For example, if player1 plays Terras Q (summoning 4 warlocks) and player 2 also plays their own copy of Terras Q (which also summons 4 Warlocks), player1's Terras Q is NOT shackled by the Warlocks that player2's Terras Q summoned.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If Terras Q leaves play and comes back, for example because of Geiger or Pasternaak's max level abilities, he comes back as a fresh copy that's treated as a totally new object. He will arrive again and summon new Warlocks, but the OLD Warlocks he summoned earlier are no longer shackling him.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If something in play becomes a copy of Terras Q, no "arrives" triggers happen so he doesn't get new Warlocks. Any Warlocks already in play do NOT shackle that copy; they only shackle the specific Terras Q whose arrives trigger summoned them.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When a unit is "destroyed" it will go to its owner's discard pile and also "die" as a consequence of that. Anything that triggers on "dies" such as the patrol zone's scavenger and technician slots, or a Soul Stone, will trigger.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Tokens count as cost 0, so this does work on token units unless you somehow have a token that is copying a higher cost unit.

rulings.author: sharpo
rulings.text: This can target units that aren't patrolling. Sidelining those won't do anything, but if they are illusions they will die from being targeted.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You can add or remove time runes from things opponents control, if you want.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You can add or remove time runes from things opponents control, if you want.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Whenever anything leaves play then comes back into play, it's treated as a fresh copy. So if this is trashed then returns to play with Geiger's or Pasternaak's max level abilities, it will get three new time runes when it returns. Also, if you can return it to your hand with Temporal Distortion, then replay it to have it arrive with three new times runes as well.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Obliterate never targets units in Codex, so it can work even on units that are untargetable. The ability that deals 4 damage to a building does target the building, so it can't hit Fox's Den School (unless you have a detector) or Hero's Monument, for example.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: "Arrives or attacks:" means you get the effect when it arrives, AND you also get the effect each time it attacks. You don't have to choose.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When Troq attacks something, his middle ability is saying to deal 1 damage to the base controlled by the same player who controls the thing he's attacking.

rulings.author: sharpo
rulings.text: If you do not reveal and discard 2 cards that cost 3, it won't target anything.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If you already have tech II units in play, it's ok to play Twilight Baron. It's just that while he is in play, you cannot play any more tech II units.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Though you can't "play" tech II units, you can still "put them into play" by any effect that's worded that way.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You can play tech II buildings and upgrades; those are not units.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If a tech II unit has forecast, such as Reaver, you still can't play it while you have Twilight Baron. You can play Reaver first, then play Twilight Baron, then have Reaver's forecast ability cause it to enter play though.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If a unit is already a dance partner from Two Step, you can't legally target it by playing another Two Step.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: "If you lose one" means if one of your partnered units leaves play or leaves your control.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You can destroy any two of the things listed in any combination. For example, you could destroy "one unit and one upgrade" or "two workers."

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Destroying a worker aways trashes it, NOT discards it.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When you destroy an opponent's worker, you don't get to choose which worker to destroy (because they're all considered identical) and you don't get to see the front of the destroyed worker.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: This doesn't cause the unit to "die", so the opponent won't draw a card if it was in the technician slot.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: The max level ability is not optional, so you must try to do as much as you can when she reaches max level. If you don't have a friendly tech 0 or I unit, you still must try to give the bonus to an opposing tech 0 or I unit, and vice versa.

rulings.author: sharpo
rulings.text: The units targeted by the max level ability will still lose the bonus and die during Vandy's owner's next upkeep, even if Vandy isn't around.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You can't use the exhaust ability the turn Verdant Tree comes under you control because it doesn't have haste.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Building tech buildings instantly means it's possible to build them all in a row in one turn. For example, you could build your tech I, then immediately build your tech II, then immediately build your tech III all in the same turn. Each tech building becomes operational right as you build it, rather than at the end of your main phase.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If you have no draw pile, looking at the top card of your draw pile does nothing. It does NOT cause you to shuffle your discard pile into your draw pile.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If you have no draw pile, you can't "exchange the top card of your draw pile with a card from your hand." Nothing happens.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: The max level ability summons a Mech token that has two time runes on it. Remove one time rune each of your upkeeps. When you remove the last, th Mech arrives. The Mech does not have haste so it can't attack the turn it arrives.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If they don't have any other ready units or heroes, they can still attack Voidblocker.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: You can attach this to an enemy unit. If you do, you still control Vortoss Emblem itself, so the time runes on it still count toward your Temporal Research.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If you have two Mimics that have flying because a THIRD unit has flying, but then that third unit dies, both your Mimics lose flying.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Units you "have" refers to units you control. It does not include units you own, but that were stolen from you for some reason, and it doesn't include units that aren't in play, such as those in Jail, Graveyard, or forecasted.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: When you put units into play with this ability, you don't have to pay for them and you don't have to meet the tech requirements for them either, so you can still do it even if you don't have a tech I or II building at all.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If you put the -1/-1 rune on an X/1 unit, that will unit will die (because it has 0 HP) even if it had armor.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: If multiple patrollers die simultaneously and the order they die would matter for some reason, then you as the active player choose that order.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: The Golgort's ability to gain a time rune triggers even if "you" deal combat damage to a building with another unit, or with a hero. It doesn't have to be with the Golgort itself.

rulings.author: Sirlin
rulings.text: Thrice-per-turn means three times per turn.
